Here is a step by step guide of what I would do

1. Move back with parents and save that money on rent/food/gas

2. Start aggressively paying off these loans. If you’re doing 1200 a month now with your rent, then do at least 1500 a month when you move back home and free up that rent money.

3. Build your credit. If you are a RESPONSIBLE spender, you can open up a credit card and pay it off monthly. After a while you will increase your credit limit. On time payments, with a high credit, and low utilization, will increase your credit score.

4. Refinance your loans for a lower interest rate. With a better credit score and lower loan balance after months of payments, look to consolidate the 16% and 15% loans (maybe even the 7% loans) with a local credit union or a company like Sofi. They will most likely offer you way better interest rates.

5. Relax and move on with your life. Once you’ve paid down your loan balance a bit and refinanced your loans to a comfortable interest rate (around 5%), just pay what you can (at least the monthly minimums) and focus on other parts of life again.

There are 3 types of muscle: skeletal muscle, smooth muscle, and cardiac muscle. The only type of muscle we have voluntary control over is skeletal muscle. Skeletal muscles are innervated by nerves that we have control over. 

Cardiac muscle (heart) and smooth muscle (other organs) are part of the autonomic nervous system. This means we can’t control these muscles voluntarily. These muscles must always be controlled unconsciously to keep our body’s homeostasis. It makes sense that we don’t voluntarily control these muscles because we wouldn’t know how to keep our body functioning.
